title: Classification of Silicate-Filled Vesicles in Pyrrhotite Grains from Asteroid Ryugu via 4DSTEM.
content: Among the utilities of 4DSTEM for investigation of materials are its ability to assess crystallinity and changes in orientation of a sample in a short acquisition time and low electron dose over small spatial scales [1,2]. Recently, 4DSTEM analysis of phyllosilicate material from asteroid Ryugu revealed d-spacing variations consistent with interlayer organic molecules [2], a finding not possible with conventional selected area electron diffraction (SAED). In comparison, we examined pyrrhotite (Fe1-xS) grains from Ryugu, which are heavily vesiculated, preserving evidence of the primordial fluid and organic material present on the asteroid during a period of aqueous activity [3,7,8]. Nanostructural evaluation of the vesicles can give insight into the origins of hydrothermal processes operating at the dawn of the solar system. Here we test the application of 4DSTEM to determining the contents of vesicles and inclusions within a pyrrhotite grain returned from asteroid Ryugu.
